title: Two installs on one Tailscale machine share the machine link and invite from the top bar
description: With only the tailscale command and the Tailscale API stubbed, up serves two fixture installs on their own ports (tailscale serve --bg --http=PORT), a rerun keeps the other install's route and a host without Tailscale gets one install instruction and carries on locally. Two served control planes on one simulated machine never read the host's machine directory: each install's master-loop sync carries the share link saved on install A (with the day it was made) into the shared machine record and back, so B shows it. Through the API (graphyard invite), an invite carries that link and a sign-in link that redeems only on its own install, once, within 24 hours under a controlled clock. In the browser each install's top-bar Invite dialog lists both installs, asks once for a Tailscale API token while nothing is saved, withholds the message naming the missing step, and copies one message with the machine link and its own address and no Graphyard sign-in link; the person's Tailscale login reaches only the install they were invited to through its serve socket, stays listed after reload and Revoke refuses them; an older link keeps its real 30-day expiry, warns in its last seven days and refuses invites once expired. The optional API token is sealed to the host in the browser, written 0600 by the host alone, never shown, masked from confined sessions, and the host makes one single-use device invite through a fake Tailscale API before the Graphyard invite, failing whole when Tailscale refuses. No Docker or Tailscale credentials.
